changes.sourceChinese: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
changes.before: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
changes.after: After Duan Liao’s defeat, Murong Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. Believing that his long-established fame and prestige would ultimately endanger his life, he feigned madness, drinking without restraint, letting his hair hang loose, and singing and shouting.
changes.reason: Restore the omitted 建威 title and the long-established fame and prestige; preserve the complete account of feigned madness.

changes.sourceChinese: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。
changes.before: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
changes.after: Earlier, when Duan Liao was defeated, Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. He thought that, because his fame and prestige had long been renowned, he would not ultimately be able to remain safe; so he feigned madness, drank without restraint, let his hair hang loose, and sang and shouted.
changes.reason: Translate 建威 as an office, rather than leaving Jianwei as an apparent personal name; retain all paired-field propositions.

changes.sourceChinese: 皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。
changes.before: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.
changes.after: Huang secretly sent the merchant Wang Che to observe Han; when Han saw Che he said nothing and only stroked his chest.
changes.reason: Restore 陰 and the explicit observation target; render 撫膺 without changing it to clutching.

changes.before: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.
changes.after: More than a hundred deserving officers were enfeoffed.
changes.reason: Proposed passive rendering preserves the unexpressed Chinese subject without silently choosing Huang as grantor. This does not resolve the held extraction event attribution.

changes.before: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.
changes.after: More than a hundred meritorious officials were enfeoffed.
changes.reason: Preserve the enfeoffment and number without supplying an unexpressed grantor; independently review in the complete imperial-grant context.

pairedFieldChecks.current: Huang sent merchant Wang Che secretly to observe Han; Han seeing Che spoke nothing, stroked his breast only.
pairedFieldChecks.result: Secretly, observe Han and stroke the breast are already explicit; preserve this field.

contextUnits.zh: 明年，釗遣其世子朝於皝。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhao sent his heir apparent to court at Huang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Gao Zhao sent his heir to pay homage to Huang.

contextUnits.zh: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.

contextUnits.zh: 歸信而不禁，故得周遊自任，至於山川形便，攻戰要路，莫不練之。

translations.literal: Gui believed and did not restrain; therefore was able to roam at will, reaching mountains and rivers’ forms and conveniences, attack and battle crucial roads—none not practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui believed the act and did not restrain him, so Han could roam at will and became thoroughly familiar with the terrain and the key routes for attack and battle.

contextUnits.zh: 皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。

translations.literal: Huang sent merchant Wang Che secretly to observe Han; Han seeing Che spoke nothing, stroked his breast only.
translations.idiomatic: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.

contextUnits.zh: 車還以白，皝曰：「翰欲來也。」

translations.literal: Che returned and reported; Huang said: “Han wishes to come.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Che reported the sign; Huang said, “He wants to come home.”

contextUnits.zh: 乃遣車遺翰弓矢，翰乃竊歸駿馬，攜其二子而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon sent Che to present Han bow and arrows; Han then stole fine horses, carried his two sons and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Che with a bow and arrows; Murong Han stole horses and rode back with his two sons.

contextUnits.zh: 使陽裕、唐柱等築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣。

translations.literal: Had Yang Yu, Tang Zhu, and others build Longcheng, construct palace and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang Yu and Tang Zhu build Longcheng, raised palaces and shrines, and renamed Liucheng county Longcheng.

contextUnits.zh: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, King of Yan; the rest of offices all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.

translations.literal: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang, Huang moved the capital to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiankang, he moved his capital to Longcheng.
